# Aetherix White Papers

> Aetherix B.V. technical white papers — NVIDIA DGX Spark, Jetson edge AI and RTX PRO systems: deployment guides, cluster setups and measured LLM and computer-vision inference benchmarks. English at the root, Dutch under /nl/.

LLM figures were measured with the CordatusAI LLM Benchmark Tool and CV
figures with the cordatus-benchmark tool. The
intelligence_index field in benchmarks.json is computed from data published by
ai-leaderboard.dev (https://www.ai-leaderboard.dev), with its method, and must be
attributed to them wherever it is shown.

## Benchmark explorers

- [LLM Inference Benchmark Explorer](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/llm-inference-benchmarks/): 131 runs — time to first token and per-request tokens/s at concurrency 1–64, with Max C (concurrent requests meeting TTFT ≤ 1 s and ≥ 20 tok/s by default) and estimated chat / agentic user capacity per model × device — how many people a model on a given device can serve. Each run's plain-language explanation is in the page HTML and in llms-full.txt. Dutch: https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/nl/llm-inference-benchmarks/
- [CV Inference Benchmark Explorer](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/cv-inference-benchmarks/): 181 device × model results — FPS per camera and frame drop by camera count. Dutch: https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/nl/cv-inference-benchmarks/
- [VLM Inference Benchmark Explorer](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/vlm-inference-benchmarks/): 137 vision-language model runs — response time (time to first token) and per-request tokens/s by image size, images per camera and number of cameras, and Max Cameras: the highest measured number of cameras (one request in flight per camera) whose answer starts within the target (3 s by default). Dutch: https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/nl/vlm-inference-benchmarks/

## Results as sentences

- [All results, explained (English and Dutch)](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/llms-full.txt): one paragraph per benchmark run — measured speed, Max C, estimated chat and agentic user capacity and what limits it; for VLM, response time and Max Cameras; for CV, FPS per camera and max cameras. Dutch pages are under /nl/.

## Raw data

- [LLM benchmarks (JSON)](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/assets/data/benchmarks.json): one entry per run; `data_points` holds `c` (concurrent requests), `ttft_ms` and `tps` (per-request output tokens/s). 128 input / 128 output tokens, ten rounds per level, mean values.
- [CV benchmarks index (JSON)](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/assets/data/cv-benchmarks/index.json): devices and models; each model's measurements are in the file named by its `path`.
- [VLM benchmarks (JSON)](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/assets/data/vlm-benchmarks.json): one entry per run; `data_points` holds one entry per measured cell — `res` (image size), `images` (per request), `c` (concurrent requests = cameras), `ttft_s` (the response time), `tps` (per-request output tokens/s), `requests` and `failed`; `models` holds each model's publisher repository and parameters.

LLM models benchmarked: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, DeepSeek-V3.1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Preview, GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.6, GLM-4.7, GLM-5, GLM-5.1, GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash, GPT-OSS 120B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, Gemma-4-31B-it, Inkling, Inkling-2-Mini, Kimi K3, Kimi-K2-Thinking, Kimi-K2.5, Kimi-K2.6, Kimi-K3.1-Pro, Laguna-S-2.1, MiMo-V2.5-Pro, MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL, MiMo-V2.6-Pro-MOPD, MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL, MiniMax-M2, MiniMax-M2.5, MiniMax-M2.7, MiniMax-M3, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B, Muse-Glimmer-30B, Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B, NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B, NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B, Nemotron-3-Ultra, Qwen3-235B-A22B, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct, Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Ripple-65B-Preview, Step-5-Preview, Tencent-Hy3, Tencent-Hy4-flash, Tencent-Hy4-preview

LLM devices: 1× DGX Spark, 2× DGX Spark, 3× DGX Spark, 4× DGX Spark, 8× DGX Spark, DGX B300, RTX PRO 6000, Thor

VLM models benchmarked: Alpamayo2-Edge, Alpamayo2-Super, Cosmos-Reason1-7B, Cosmos-Reason2-2B, Cosmos-Reason2-8B, Cosmos3-Edge, Cosmos3-Nano, Eagle2.5-8B, Fara1.5-27B, GLM-4.6V-Flash, Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, Gemma-4-31B-it, Gemma-4-E2B-it, Gemma-4-E4B-it, Granite-Vision-4.1-4B, H2O-Lightning-4B, Inkling-2-Mini, LFM2.5-VL-3B, LensVLM-9B, Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Nano-VL-8B, Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct, MedGemma-1.5-4B-it, MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B, MiniCPM-V-4.6, MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B, MiniCPM-V-4.7-35B-A3B, Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603, NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B, NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B, Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL, Qwen-Drive-1.0-4B, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct, Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, Qwen3.5-0.8B, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3.5-2B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Qwen3.8-27B, d1-3B

## White papers

- [DGX Spark 2-Node AI Cluster Setup Guide](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/dgx-spark-2node-cluster-setup/): Point-to-point topology AI cluster setup with 2 NVIDIA DGX Spark nodes: management and compute networks, RoCEv2/RDMA, sparkrun configuration.
- [DGX Spark 3-Node AI Cluster Setup Guide](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/dgx-spark-3node-cluster-setup/): Ring (mesh) topology AI cluster setup with 3 NVIDIA DGX Spark nodes: management and compute networks, RoCEv2/RDMA, sparkrun configuration.
- [DGX Spark 4-Node AI Cluster Setup Guide](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/dgx-spark-4node-cluster-setup/): Switch-based AI cluster setup with 4 NVIDIA DGX Spark nodes over a MikroTik CRS812: management and compute networks, RoCEv2/RDMA, sparkrun and NAS.
- [DGX Spark 8-Node AI Cluster Setup Guide](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/dgx-spark-8node-cluster-setup/): Switch-based AI cluster setup with 8 NVIDIA DGX Spark nodes over a MikroTik CRS804 with 200G breakout: management and compute networks, RoCEv2/RDMA, sparkrun and NAS.
- [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 4× DGX Spark Deployment](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/deepseek-v4.1-flash-4spark-deployment/): Deployment of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (763B MoE, FP8, DSpark k=5) on 4× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10) with tensor parallelism: vLLM build chain, 7 SM 12.1a patches, Engram-on-disk, benchmark results and B300 comparison.
- [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 8× DGX Spark TP8 Deployment](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/deepseek-v4.1-flash-8spark-deployment/): Deployment of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (763B MoE, FP8, DSpark k=5) on 8× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10) with TP8: two configurations (300K Engram-in-memory, 1M Engram-on-disk), NCCL optimization, benchmark results and TP4 comparison.
- [Engram Offloading in LLM Inference](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/conditional-memory-offloading/): Engram tables are large but read only a few rows per token, so they can move from GPU memory to host RAM or NVMe. What that means on DGX Spark, RTX PRO 6000 and DGX B300, and measured results with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.
- [KV Cache Offloading with LMCache in LLM Inference](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/kv-cache-offloading-lmcache/): What LMCache adds to vLLM when the same contexts come back: a three-tier KV cache (GPU, CPU, NVMe) on DGX Spark, measured TTFT — 1.95× on repeated access, 3.3× after a service restart — and the settings and limits that come with it.
- [Kimi K3 Inference Benchmark on DGX-B300](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/kimi-k3-dgx-b300-inference-benchmark/): Performance evaluation of Moonshot AI Kimi K3 (2.8T MoE, MXFP4) on NVIDIA DGX-B300 (8x Blackwell Ultra, TP=8): vLLM vs SGLang, direct vs DSpark speculative decoding, with SLO-driven capacity planning.
- [LLM Quantization Selection Guide](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/llm-quantization-selection/): Decision guide for LLM quantization: how workload, quantization format, GPU architecture and checkpoint reliability decide the choice — with the selection flow, frequent mistakes, case examples and a quick command reference.
- [Local LLM Usage Guide](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/local-llm-guide/): End-to-end decision guide for local LLM usage: hardware (NVIDIA Jetson, RTX PRO, DGX Spark, DGX/HGX), model selection, software stack and scenario mapping.
- [NVIDIA DGX B300 vs GB300 NVL72 Cluster Architecture Comparison](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/b300-gb300-cluster-architecture/): Technical comparison of two NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra architectures, DGX B300 and GB300 NVL72: system design, scaling approach, network fabric, power and cooling, and which workloads suit which platform.
- [Network Link Speed for Tensor-Parallel Inference on DGX Sparks (200G vs 100G)](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/dgx-spark-link-speed-tensor-parallel/): How much network bandwidth a tensor-parallel DGX Spark cluster really uses, and what running each DGX Spark at 100G instead of 200G costs: the mechanism, an estimate from the model's architecture, and measurements with GLM-5.3 at TP8 and with GLM-5.3-Flash at TP4 on real 100G links.
- [Qwen3.6-27B DGX Spark Benchmark](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/qwen3.6-27b-dgx-spark-benchmark/): Performance evaluation of the Qwen3.6-27B model on the NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10) platform with FP8, FP8-MTP, AWQ-MTP, NVFP4, and NVFP4-MTP quantization variants.
- [Qwen3.6-27B DGX Spark Cluster Scaling](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/qwen3.6-27b-dgx-spark-scaling/): Multi-node scaling study of Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 on 1x, 2x, and 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10): tensor parallelism over 200GbE, SLO-driven capacity planning, and TP-vs-replication deployment guidance.
- [System One in Production: Decision Quality, Reliability and Performance on DGX Spark with vLLM and SGLang](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/system-one-production-readiness/): Six typed-decision models from 0.6B to 27B evaluated on one NVIDIA DGX Spark with vLLM and SGLang: Turkish accuracy, confidence calibration, paraphrase consistency, multimodal limits, engine portability, and the confidence thresholds a production decision policy needs.
- [The First Open-Weight Alternatives to Jev](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/jev-open-weight-alternatives/): Six open-weight typed-decision models compared on one NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10) through a shared state + questions interface and one 25-question set: accuracy, calibration, option-order sensitivity and latency — and which model fits which job.

## Other pages

- [About](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/about/): Aetherix B.V. — Netherlands-based provider of NVIDIA Jetson hardware for edge AI.
- [Changelog](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/changelog/): What is new on the site: new white papers and new LLM, VLM and CV benchmark results.
- [Device Advisor](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/device-advisor/): Describe your cameras and pick a vision-language model, and this page names the smallest device we have measured that keeps up — then plays the stream back as a live timeline, so you can see how often each camera is answered and how many of its frames the model ever sees.
- [Home](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/): Aetherix B.V. technical white papers — NVIDIA DGX Spark, Jetson edge AI and RTX PRO systems: deployment guides, cluster setups and measured inference benchmarks.
- [White Papers](https://whitepapers.aetherix.com/papers/): Aetherix technical white paper list.
